name: World
description: Awareness of the outside and interaction with it: public science, the tools of the outside, the models the hub asks, and how current the hub's own research is. Its metrics move when something outside the system changes.
purpose: Bring in what is outside the system and let the AI act on it through the best available tool.
approach: Admit tools and data sources through narrow interfaces and compare each candidate on the same tasks.
out_of_scope: What the system keeps internally and which parts of the outside a particular system has declared as its own.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-the-world has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-world chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Task pass rate and cost per passing task, per hub.
inputs: A query, and whether papers are wanted.
outputs: Material from outside the system, with its sources, and the result of using an outside tool.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-world", "latest Rust version")` brings in what the outside says, through Tools.

name: The Self
description: Keeps the five kinds of part working as one whole: the Assembler builds them and reports the coverage, Integrity keeps the whole honest and generic and audits the run record, and Role Understanding says what each part is for. Responds to a request by running the flow through Consciousness, Body, Intelligence and World's tools; no answer is made up when a part is missing.
purpose: Keep every part working as one whole for one request.
approach: Compose Integrity, Role Understanding and the Assembler, and call the other four containers in the order the flow says: Consciousness represents the person, Body declares where the data lives, Intelligence processes the request, Body keeps the run record and Integrity audits it.
out_of_scope: How information is processed, where the system's data lives, what the outside offers and what each person wants.
milestones: 1. The whole answers a real request as one capable assistant (metric-the-self).
measures_of_success: The whole answers a real request as one capable assistant.
inputs: A request, and the person it is for.
outputs: A response to a request, with the step of every part that took part and an honest account of the steps that have no arm yet.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-self", "Explain what Judgment Calls decides for a person")` runs the whole flow; the same call as `hubofhubs.run("hub-of-hubs", ...)`.

name: Body
description: The AI system's form and internal context. Every part here is specified to expect adaptation to a particular system, by an adapter or by a declaration of the system's data and integrations.
purpose: Let the hub apply to one particular system by declaring where its data lives, where its requests come from and which of its integrations the AI may use, and keep the run record, the configuration, the environment variables, the secrets and the stored authentication the tools need.
approach: Compose Internal Context, Intake Sources and Hands, and let a system declare what is its own: where its data lives, where its requests come from and which integrations it already depends on.
out_of_scope: Reading or writing the data (a World tool does that), finding the right context for a request, and the tools of the outside.
milestones: 1. A system declares its own sources and acts through the hub without code written for each part (metric-the-body).
measures_of_success: A system declares its own sources and acts through the hub without code written for each part.
inputs: Nothing.
outputs: What a particular system declares about its own data and integrations.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-body", ...)` describes the system's declared sources, intake and integrations and keeps the run record.

name: Intelligence
description: How information is processed for one request: the long view is read, the request becomes a measurable goal, the Mind plans and writes the response from what the Subconscious and the World bring, and the result is checked for goal completion and response quality.
purpose: Turn one request and what is known into a response that meets its goal.
approach: Compose Mind, Higher Mind, Subconscious and Critical Thinking in the order the flow says, with Nervous System and Judgment Calls before a risky piece and Proactivity starting standing work.
out_of_scope: Where the system's data lives, the tools of the outside, and what a person wants (the Representative carries that).
milestones: 1. One request is answered from the information that bears on it and no more (metric-the-intelligence).
measures_of_success: One request is answered from the information that bears on it and no more.
inputs: A request and the Representative it is for.
outputs: A response to one request, with the step of every part that took part.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-intelligence", {"request": ..., "person": ...})` processes one request with the Representative's authority.

name: Consciousness
description: The humans who interact with the system: AI Representatives act for a person, Prioritization turns the person's priorities into ESOI, Judgment Calls decide when to ask that person, and Feedback Learning applies the person's feedback to specs and metrics.
purpose: Keep the system aligned with the humans and policies it works for.
approach: Compose Representatives, Request Intake, Prioritization, Judgment Calls and Feedback Learning, on one signal contract with the Nervous System.
out_of_scope: Raising the risk signal, judging response quality against a profile, and storing what the system remembers.
milestones: 1. A representative asks a person when that person would want to be asked and acts as the person wants (metric-the-consciousness).
measures_of_success: A representative asks a person when that person would want to be asked and acts as the person wants.
inputs: A person, and their feedback when there is some.
outputs: The person's Representative, and what the system learned from that person.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-consciousness", ...)` returns the person's Representative and priorities.

name: Hands
description: Makes sure a system's enduring integrations, such as an enterprise system's own AI tool registry, its LLM platform and its guardrails, are appropriately accessible to the system and used by it. The language models and guardrails themselves come from World, and generic tool calling such as MCP belongs to World as well. Specified to expect adaptation to a particular system.
purpose: Make the integrations a system already depends on accessible to the AI and actually used.
approach: Read the system's declaration of its integrations, check that each is reachable by the AI, and report the ones that are declared but unused.
out_of_scope: Calling a tool (Tools does that), supplying the models and guardrails (World and Model Plumbing do that), and measuring how much code a connection needs (a metric of Tools).
milestones: 1. A declared enterprise integration is reachable by the AI and used (metric-integration-added-with-zero-code).
measures_of_success: Per-integration code changes (target 0); days from a hub listing an integration to a user connecting it; credential isolation checks all pass.
inputs: A system's declared integrations.
outputs: Which of the system's enduring integrations are accessible to the AI and which are used.
effects: Reads the registry's connection rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Feedback Learning
description: Applies a person's feedback to the specs and metrics, not to the instructions of every task, so a correction given once is followed afterwards. It proposes quality profile changes, which ESOI Application applies as spec and metric edits.
purpose: Make a correction given once change behaviour afterwards: propose edits to specs and metrics, which ESOI Application applies directly unless Judgment Calls decides to ask.
approach: Record each piece of feedback against what it corrected and adjust the behaviour it concerns.
out_of_scope: Applying the edit (ESOI Application does that), deciding the profile the person prefers (Representatives own it) and the thresholds for asking (Judgment Calls owns them).
milestones: 1. A correction given once is followed afterwards (metric-feedback-learning).
measures_of_success: A correction given once is followed afterwards.
inputs: A person's feedback.
outputs: Proposed edits to specs and metrics.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Critical Thinking
description: Turns a request into a measurable target, and holds the result to it. ESOI Application creates and edits the specs and metrics and runs the improvement loop, Metric Translation turns a request into a metric with a target, Goal Completion says whether the goal was met, and Response Quality judges the response against a quality profile.
purpose: Say what success means for a request and check that it was reached.
approach: Translate the request into a metric, then check the goal and the response quality, each as its own solution.
out_of_scope: Planning and writing the response (the Mind does that), keeping a person's preferences (Representatives do that) and deciding when to ask (Judgment Calls do that).
milestones: 1. The evidence check runs on written answers with and without supporting links. 2. A second arm exists beside it. 3. The selected arm was chosen by the seat's metric.
measures_of_success: Share of unsupported links in written answers that are reported, with no supported link reported.
inputs: A request, its response, the objective and the quality profile.
outputs: A target for a request, whether its goal was met and how good the response is.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: Pass the answer and the evidence text: critique(answer, evidence).

name: Subconscious
description: Finds and prepares information for the Mind. It reads the system's context only through Internal Context; Cards From Files builds the cards, the Context Retriever picks the cards and file pieces a request needs within a token budget, and Intuition offers what comes to mind unasked.
purpose: Give the Mind the information a request needs and nothing from another person's scope: cards, file chunks and memory, found and prepared.
approach: Read what Internal Context returns, pick what bears on the request with the Context Retriever within the scope of the asker, and hand the Mind the cards, the pieces and what Intuition offers, with a step for each.
out_of_scope: Retaining memories (Long-Term Memory does that), storing cards and run records (Internal Context does that) and bringing in the outside (World does that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-subconscious has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-the-subconscious has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-subconscious chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Right context admitted, nothing from another scope.
inputs: A query, and optionally a folder's files and a token budget.
outputs: The cards, the file pieces and what Intuition offered for a request, with the step of each part.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-subconscious", "rust release")` recalls the cards; `prepare` returns what the Mind is handed.

name: Mind
description: What the planning and responding AI can see for one request and how it outputs plans, requests and communications. Context Intake takes in what the Subconscious and the World bring, the Planner breaks the request into pieces, Delegation hands each piece to the right worker only when that is necessary, and the Response Writer outputs the plan, request or communication.
purpose: Turn one request and its context into a plan and a response.
approach: Run the four parts in order, and check the Nervous System signal and Judgment Calls before a risky step.
out_of_scope: Finding the information (Subconscious and World do that), the long view across requests (Higher Mind), deciding whether the goal was met (Critical Thinking) and deciding when to ask a person (Judgment Calls).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-mind has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-the-mind has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-mind chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Answer quality per dollar and per second.
parameters: A model-call seat and a tier-selection seat (built on first use, so a prompt with no tier never asks for it).
inputs: A request, its target, the Representative's authority and the guidance, when there is some.
outputs: A plan, request or communication for one request, with the step of every part of the Mind.
effects: One model call per request, which costs what the provider charges or draws on the operator's subscription.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-mind", {"request": ...})` plans, delegates and writes for one request.

name: Higher Mind
description: The long view across requests: Long-Term Memory retains and recalls what happened, Objectives holds the live hierarchy of intents and goals, and Guidance gives the Planner an infrequent longer-term nudge.
purpose: Keep the AI working toward what matters beyond the request in front of it.
approach: Read Objectives, Long-Term Memory and Guidance for one request and hand the result to the Planner and Critical Thinking.
out_of_scope: Finding the information a single request needs (Subconscious does that) and planning one request (the Mind does that).
milestones: 1. The long view survives from one request to the next (metric-higher-mind).
measures_of_success: The long view survives from one request to the next.
inputs: A request and the person.
outputs: What the AI remembers, what it is working toward and the nudge it should take.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("higher-mind", {"request": ...})` returns the objectives, the memory and the nudge for a request.

name: Role Understanding
description: Each part of the system knows what it is for, what it hands on and what it leaves to the others, so no part does another part's work or hides a failure of its own.
purpose: Give every part a role in the whole that the part and the Assembler can both read.
approach: State each part's role as data the part and the Assembler can read, and compare what a part does with the role it states.
out_of_scope: Building the parts, and deciding which arm of a part is best.
milestones: 1. A part's behaviour matches the role the whole gives it (metric-role-understanding).
measures_of_success: A part's behaviour matches the role the whole gives it.
inputs: The id of a part.
outputs: The role of a part (purpose, what it is not responsible for, who owns that) read from its record.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Model Plumbing
description: The one measured path every part uses to ask a model: the Model Tier Chooser picks the model for a tier and the Vendor Model Caller reaches the vendor and steps to the next provider when one fails.
purpose: Give every part one measured path to a model, so cost and failover are chosen once, and spend the model calls of the goal record's budget.
approach: Choose the measured model for the tier, ask it through the vendor caller and report the text.
out_of_scope: What to ask the model (each part does that), writing the response (the Response Writer does that) and the language models themselves, which are the vendors'.
milestones: 1. Every part asks a model through one measured path (metric-model-plumbing).
measures_of_success: Every part asks a model through one measured path.
inputs: A prompt and a tier.
outputs: The model's answer to a prompt at a tier.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("model-plumbing", {"prompt": ..., "tier": "cheap"})` asks the model measured best for the tier.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Science
description: Looks up what public research says and returns observations a reader can cite.
purpose: Bring in public science a reader can check.
approach: Search the strongest sources available and return their findings as citable observations.
out_of_scope: Searching the web in general (Web Search does that) and reading a person's own data (Internal Context declares where it is and File Reading reads it).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-science has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The staged stage of metric-the-science has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The whole stage of metric-the-science has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 4. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-science chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Claims supported by sources; evidence weighed.
parameters: The web-search a search arm needs, an optional API key and contact address for the scholarly service, and a timeout.
inputs: One query or a list of queries with an optional result limit and a freshness flag; or a page address with an optional focus, part and full flag.
outputs: Observations of papers, with their sources.
effects: Makes network requests to the scholarly service or the web and keeps a short cache; counts calls against a daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: Pass a query and read the hits of the returned observation, each with a link a reader can check.
verdict_detail: openalex_semantic leads openalex (openalex 0.05 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.019, 12 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic leads openalex_keywords (openalex_keywords 0.075 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0234, 13 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic leads openalex_keywords_model (openalex_keywords_model 0.075 against openalex_semantic 0.3; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.0234, 11 of 40 cases disagree; one of 3 looks, alpha 0.0167); openalex_semantic is better than openalex_semantic_and_web (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=6.2e-31, 150 of 150 cases disagree); openalex_semantic is better than web_research (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.12e-25, 150 of 150 cases disagree)

name: Tools
description: What the AI can use or do outside the system, grouped by category. A category is a solution and its integrations are its implementations, and every implementation of a category does the same job. Web Search, File Reading, File Editing, Connected System Operations and Delegated Agent Sessions are the categories.
purpose: Let the AI use the best tool of each category (web search, reading files, editing files, connected systems, agent sessions) without a product wiring each one, refusing a category the Representative's authority does not allow and data outside its data scope.
approach: Choose the best integration of each category by measurement, and keep the long tail as registry entries.
out_of_scope: Which tool the system's own data uses (Internal Context declares that), judging whether a goal was met (Goal Completion does that) and the system's enduring integrations (Hands does that).
milestones: 1. The best integration of each category is chosen by measurement (metric-the-tools).
measures_of_success: The best integration of each category is chosen by measurement.
inputs: A category and a request.
outputs: The result of using a tool, by category.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-tools", {"category": "web-search", "request": "latest Rust version"})` uses the tool of a category, refusing one the authority does not allow.

name: Intake Sources
description: Declares where this system's requests come from (a chat, a task queue, a place where meeting action items are written) and reads the requests waiting at each, handing each over once. The hub ships the folder queue; a system declares its own adapter.
purpose: Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system.
approach: Offer one adapter shape for a source of requests (list the sources, pull what waits at one, each handed over once) and let a system declare its own adapter; the hub ships a folder queue.
out_of_scope: Deciding who a request is from and what to do with it (Request Intake and the flow do that) and reading or writing the system's other data (Internal Context does that).
milestones: 1. Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system. (authoritative metric metric-intake-sources).
measures_of_success: Let a system say where its requests come from and read them, without the hub being written for that system.
inputs: A source name and a limit.
outputs: The declared sources, and the requests waiting at one of them.
effects: Reads the declared source and removes each request it hands over.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("intake-sources", {"source": "", "limit": 10})` takes the waiting requests.

name: Internal Context
description: Declares where the system's data lives and which World tool reads it. The default is local files at a folder the system names, read through File Reading. A system that keeps its data elsewhere declares that instead, with its own tool, through an adapter. The Subconscious reads the system's context only through here, and the run record goes to the run store, apart from the kept cards.
purpose: Let the AI know what a particular system knows, without the hub being written for that system: the declaration of where its data lives and whether each source belongs to the system or to a person, the configuration its tools need, and the run record the flow writes.
approach: Offer one declaration for each internal source, read it through the tool the declaration names, and keep what is read as cards; keep run records in a separate run store.
out_of_scope: Reading or writing files and operations (World tools do that), retaining or recalling memories (Long-Term Memory does that), choosing the context a request needs (Subconscious does that) and proposing cards from files (Cards From Files does that).
milestones: 1. An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI (metric-internal-context).
measures_of_success: An internal source is declared once and its context reaches the AI.
inputs: A query.
outputs: The declared sources of the system's data, the cards that match a query, every readable item as text by id, and the run record id.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("internal-context", "rust release")` returns the matching cards; `corpus` returns everything readable.

name: Judgment Calls
description: Decides, for one person, whether to ask, proceed or decline when the Nervous System raises a risk signal. The decision may go to a human, to another agent or to a delegate. It shares one signal contract with the Nervous System.
purpose: Ask a person only when that person would want to be asked, and decide how: whether the ask blocks or waits, whether it is batched, what may continue meanwhile, and whether a change to specs or a learning step needs an ask at all (by default it does not).
approach: Take a risk signal with its severity and reason, decide per person, and let feedback move the thresholds.
out_of_scope: Raising the risk signal (the Nervous System does that) and learning the person's thresholds from feedback (Feedback Learning does that).
milestones: 1. The decision matches what the person would have chosen (metric-judgment-calls).
measures_of_success: The decision matches what the person would have chosen.
inputs: A risk signal with its severity and reason, and the person.
outputs: One decision for one person: ask, proceed or decline, and who is asked.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("judgment-calls", {"signal": {"severity": "high", "reason": "a deletion"}, "person": ""})` returns ask, proceed or decline for that person.
verdict_detail: severity_policy leads ask_every_time (ask_every_time 0.944 against severity_policy 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.125, 4 of 72 cases disagree)

name: Prioritization
description: Translates a person's priorities, which are sometimes only subtly specified or implied, into ESOI: milestones, metric weights and quality profile weights, and puts the work that competes for attention (tasks, asks, standing-work triggers) in order for that person, with the reason for each place and the priority in the form Metric Translation and the Planner use. ESOI is the structure in which prioritization is carried out. It works with Critical Thinking, Representatives, Guidance and Proactivity.
purpose: Turn the priorities a person implies into ESOI.
approach: Read the candidates' own fields (the person's own rank, deadline, who is waiting, what blocks it, when it was asked, when the person was last nudged) and what the person stated or implied (an explicit order, what to defer, what their feedback implies, quality weights), order the candidates by the rules the person stated and the fields carry, and restate each priority as a weighted milestone, so Critical Thinking and the Planner can use it. Proactivity asks it what matters first among the work that is due, and Consciousness gives its answer to Intelligence.
out_of_scope: Carrying the person's preferences (Representatives do that), turning a request into a metric (Metric Translation does that), long-term nudges (Guidance does that), deciding what is due (Proactivity does that) and whether work may be done unasked (Judgment Calls does that).
milestones: 1. The weights the system derives match the priorities the person confirms (authoritative metric metric-human-prioritization).
measures_of_success: The weights the system derives match the priorities the person confirms.
inputs: A person, a request, the candidates with the fields their data carries, what the person stated or implied, and the time.
outputs: The candidates in order, each with its place, the reason in words and a metric-ready priority (milestone, weight, due, criterion); the candidates the person's constraints hold back with why; and the quality profile weights.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: the arms are pure functions of what they are given.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("prioritization", {"person": "...", "candidates": [...], "stated": {...}, "now": "2026-07-12T09:00:00Z"})` returns the ordered candidates.
verdict_detail: stated_fields is better than as_given (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.000488, 12 of 13 cases disagree)

name: Representatives
description: The AI personas that act for a person or a team. A Representative carries the person's authority, preferences and quality profile into every request, and the sub-goals of that request carry the same authority.
purpose: Let an AI act for a person the way that person would want, within the authority the person gave: the worker categories allowed, the data scope (whose data the AI may read), the person's asking policy and quality profile.
approach: Give each representative the person's judgment about asking and the person's feedback.
out_of_scope: Deciding when to ask (Judgment Calls does that), learning from feedback (Feedback Learning does that) and translating implied priorities (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. A representative acts as its person would want (metric-the-representatives).
measures_of_success: A representative acts as its person would want.
inputs: A person.
outputs: The person's authority, preferences and quality profile for a request.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-representatives", "")` returns the person's authority, data scope and preferences.

name: Request Intake
description: Takes in the requests people make from every source Body declares and attaches each to the person who made it, so the rest of the flow can ask for that person's Representative.
purpose: Take in every request a person makes, once, from wherever the system listens.
approach: For each source Body declares, pull the waiting requests once, attach each to the person it is from, and hand them to the flow.
out_of_scope: Where requests come from (Body's Intake Sources define the adapters), answering them (the flow does that) and what each person is allowed (Representatives do that).
milestones: 1. Take in every request a person makes, once, from wherever the system listens. (authoritative metric metric-request-intake).
measures_of_success: Take in every request a person makes, once, from wherever the system listens.
inputs: Which sources to read, and optionally one person.
outputs: A list of requests, each with its text, person and source.
effects: Reads the sources through Intake Sources and takes each request out of its source so it is handed over once.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("request-intake", {"person": ""})` returns the waiting requests.

name: ESOI Application
description: Creates and edits specs and metrics, applies the structure's principles and runs the iterative improvement loop, so what a request needs becomes a measured specification rather than a longer prompt.
purpose: Apply ESOI to the system's own specs and metrics: an AI is the author of the specs, and a proposed edit is applied directly unless Judgment Calls decides to ask.
approach: Create and edit the specs and metrics of the system by the ESOI principles, as edits to records and never as longer prompts, and run the improvement loop on a metric.
out_of_scope: Choosing the metric for a request (Metric Translation does that) and proposing edits from feedback (Feedback Learning does that).
milestones: 1. A spec or metric edited by the loop scores no worse on its own measure afterwards (authoritative metric metric-esoi-application).
measures_of_success: A spec or metric edited by the loop scores no worse on its own measure afterwards.
inputs: A proposed change to a spec or metric.
outputs: Edited specs and metrics, and a run of the improvement loop.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Long-Term Memory
description: The retention policy and the recall over the Body's store: what the system keeps across requests, for how long, and how it is found again.
purpose: Let the AI keep and recall what happened across requests.
approach: Keep dated records of what happened and recall them by relevance and recency.
out_of_scope: Where the data is stored (Internal Context declares that) and finding information for one request (Subconscious does that).
milestones: 1. A later request can use what an earlier one learned (metric-long-term-memory).
measures_of_success: A later request can use what an earlier one learned.
inputs: A query and the person.
outputs: Remembered events that bear on a request.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Objectives
description: The live hierarchy of intents and goals across requests. A new request is placed under the objective it serves, and a goal rolls up to its parent.
purpose: Let the AI keep working toward a goal over many requests and know which objective a request serves.
approach: Record each objective with its done-standard and check progress against it.
out_of_scope: Turning a request into a metric (Metric Translation does that) and nudging the Planner (Guidance does that).
milestones: 1. An objective persists and progress is checked against its done-standard (metric-live-objectives).
measures_of_success: An objective persists and progress is checked against its done-standard.
inputs: The person.
outputs: The objectives in progress, their hierarchy and their state.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Guidance
description: An infrequent, longer-term nudge to the Planner, drawn from the objectives and memory, and the context-specific criteria for what a good response is in this situation.
purpose: Keep the Planner pointed at the longer-term outcome without taking over the request.
approach: Hold an infrequent, longer-term nudge for the planning of a request and the quality criteria that belong to the context, derived from the objectives and the memory, and give a nudge only when one is due.
out_of_scope: Planning (the Planner does that), a person's own preferences (the Representative carries those) and translating implied priorities (Prioritization does that).
milestones: 1. A nudge is infrequent and moves the Planner toward the longer-term outcome (authoritative metric metric-planner-guidance).
measures_of_success: A nudge is infrequent and moves the Planner toward the longer-term outcome.
inputs: A request and the objectives.
outputs: A nudge for the Planner, or nothing when none is due, and context-specific quality criteria.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Nervous System
description: Watches a run and raises at most one small risk signal, with a severity and a reason, when a step cannot be undone or belongs to a person, and leaves ordinary work alone. The signal goes to Judgment Calls.
purpose: Send one risk signal, a severity and a reason, before irreversible or person-owned steps, without slowing ordinary work and without routing.
approach: Read a short digest of each step by rule and send one risk signal: high for a step a person should authorize, medium for a step the rules cannot classify, none for plain reading.
out_of_scope: Deciding whether to ask a particular person (Judgment Calls does that), routing a run (the Planner and Delegation do that) and carrying out the step (the tools do that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-nervous-system has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The measured stage of metric-nervous-system has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-nervous-system chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Risks caught against false alarms, and latency.
parameters: The rules the consumer replaces to carry its own policy (the classes of consent and the read and consent actions).
inputs: A short digest of the run.
outputs: One risk signal: a severity (none, low, medium or high) and a reason; it never raises and never routes.
effects: None beyond the signal: the arm reads a digest by rule and makes no model call.
usage_notes: The signal goes to Judgment Calls, which decides for the person; the overseer that routed a running worker five ways is a helper of Delegation, not an arm of this seat.
verdict_detail: consent_gate leads none (none 0.65 against consent_gate 0.743; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.718, 52 of 60 cases disagree); consent_gate leads overseer (overseer 0.917 against consent_gate 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.718, overseer passed 33 of 36, consent_gate 36 of 36); consent_gate leads two_stage (two_stage 0.944 against consent_gate 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact Fisher test on the pass counts (no per-case rows), Holm-adjusted p=0.718, two_stage passed 34 of 36, consent_gate 36 of 36)

name: Proactivity
description: Says which of the system's standing schedules are due, by calendar period in their own zone, by a requested run or by an event since the last run, so the system acts without being asked.
purpose: Let the system start its standing work when it is due, without being asked.
approach: Given the system's standing schedules and the time, say which are due and as what request, so the Planner can plan them; each trigger says its kind (a requested run, an event, a calendar period or elapsed time). Events of a consumer's own come through Body's Intake Sources and are attached to the schedules that name their source. The due work and the other work waiting go to Prioritization, which says what matters first, and the triggers come back in that order. The arms differ in how due is decided (calendar, event or elapsed hours).
out_of_scope: Doing the work (the flow does that) and deciding whether it may be done unasked (Judgment Calls and the Nervous System do that).
milestones: 1. Let the system start its standing work when it is due, without being asked. (authoritative metric metric-proactivity).
measures_of_success: Let the system start its standing work when it is due, without being asked.
inputs: The schedules, the time, the events pulled from Intake Sources and, optionally, a Prioritization answer.
outputs: The triggers that are due, in priority order when Prioritization was asked: schedule, kind, reason, the request to run, and rank, priority reason and metric.
effects: Reads the schedules it is given and the time; it starts nothing itself.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("proactivity", {"schedules": [...], "now": "2026-07-12T09:00:00Z"})` returns the due triggers; docs/how-to/build-an-autopilot-on-the-hub.md builds a whole autopilot on it.
verdict_detail: calendar_and_events is better than elapsed_hours (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.00781, 8 of 18 cases disagree)

name: Intuition
description: What comes to mind for a request without being asked for: cards and facts the Subconscious offers because they are close to the request, which the Mind may take or ignore.
purpose: Let useful information surface unasked.
approach: Offer the closest items to a request, within a budget, and let the Mind take or ignore them.
out_of_scope: Answering a query (the Context Retriever does that).
milestones: 1. An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept (metric-the-intuition).
measures_of_success: An offered item is useful often enough that it is kept.
inputs: A request and a limit.
outputs: Items offered to the Mind for a request.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: No arm yet: the seat is defined and empty.

name: Assembler
description: Builds every seat from its selected arm and reports which seats are built and, for each that is not, the line that says exactly what to pass or set. It runs nothing for a request.
purpose: Build the whole from the best-measured arm of every seat and report its coverage, with no glue written by the consumer.
approach: Resolve each seat's selected arm and its needs, build what can be built and report what is still pending.
out_of_scope: Running a request (The Self does that), deciding what a part does, and judging whether a response is good.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-the-assembler has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The production stage of metric-the-assembler has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-the-assembler chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: End-to-end pass rate on a production consumer.
inputs: Free text.
outputs: Which seats are built, which are pending with the line that says what to pass or set, and the share built.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-assembler", {})` reports the coverage of the hub from the environment it is given.

name: Integrity
description: Keeps the hub generic: claims match evidence, records match code, and only failures that are hidden are reported. Audits the hub for consumer wording and how stale its research is. A documented default is never an integrity finding.
purpose: Keep the whole honest and usable by any consumer: what the system says about itself and what it did matches the record.
approach: Audit what the hub says about itself against what it holds and did: consumer wording found by scan, the steps of a run record that do not say why they did not run, and answers given with no Response Writer step.
out_of_scope: Judging whether an answer to a person is good (Response Quality does that), fixing what it finds, and choosing which arm is best.
milestones: 1. Consumer-specific strings found by the scan: none (metric-system-integrity).
measures_of_success: Consumer-specific strings found by scan (target 0).
inputs: The terms that count as consumer wording.
outputs: Consumer-specific strings found, the findings against a run record, stale areas and the share of connections that need no code.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("system-integrity", ["examplevendor"])` audits the hub for the terms given; `audit_run` audits one run record.

name: Learning
description: Reports which of the hub's research areas are out of date: the areas whose last research is older than ninety days, read through the Research Freshness Reader. Its metric moves when the outside changes. Doing the research again is a separate, scheduled job outside this part.
purpose: Keep what the hub recommends current with the outside.
approach: Read the recorded research date of each area and report the areas whose last research is older than the bar, so a person or a process can research them again.
out_of_scope: Doing the research (a scheduled refresh outside this part does that) and judging whether a recommendation is still best (the metric of each solution does that).
milestones: 1. Every seat's last_researched is inside the 90-day refresh window (metric-the-learning).
measures_of_success: Days since each seat was last researched and compared.
inputs: An ISO date (today when none is given).
outputs: The areas whose research is stale.
effects: Reads the registry's dated rows; writes nothing and makes no call.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("the-learning", "2026-11-03")` lists the stale areas as of that day.

name: Card Store
description: A small store that keeps cards, the hub's own memory unit, and finds them again by words or a tag.
purpose: Keep cards and find them again.
approach: Store each card under its id and search by every word of the query.
out_of_scope: Building the cards from files (Cards From Files does that) and choosing which cards a request needs (the Context Retriever does that).
milestones: 1. Every case passes: cards found again by words, nothing lost on a repeated add (metric-card-store).
measures_of_success: Cards found again by words; nothing lost on a second add of the same id.
parameters: The store location (in memory or one SQLite file).
inputs: A card to add, a card id, and a query with an optional tag and a result limit.
outputs: The id of an added card, a card or nothing for an id, the cards matching a query or a tag, whether a delete removed one, and the count.
effects: Writes and deletes cards in the store (a SQLite file when one is named); reads nothing else.
usage_notes: Default arm is local SQLite, in memory or one file.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Goal Completion
description: Says whether the goal condition of a request or sub-goal was met, against the done-standard its metric names. It is a machine learning task, and it is not the judgment of how good the response is.
purpose: Check that the goal was met.
approach: Compare the outcome of a goal with its done-standard, reading the outcome's own structured facts (its coverage, its errors, its refusals) before any prose, and say met or not with a reason.
out_of_scope: Judging how good the response is (Response Quality does that) and making the change (the tools do that).
milestones: 1. The verdict on whether a goal was met matches the verdict of a reviewer (authoritative metric metric-goal-completion).
measures_of_success: The verdict on whether a goal was met matches the verdict of a reviewer.
inputs: A goal, its done-standard and the outcome.
outputs: Whether the goal was met, with the reason.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("goal-completion", {"goal": ..., "done_standard": ..., "outcome": ...})` returns met and the reason; a worker that failed or was refused is never met.
verdict_detail: evidence_standard leads nonempty (nonempty 0.786 against evidence_standard 1; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=0.25, 3 of 14 cases disagree)

name: Metric Translation
description: Turns a request into a metric with a target value or an improvement, adjustable in real time, and applies the same step recursively to each sub-goal, rolling each up to its parent objective.
purpose: Make what success means for a request explicit and measurable as a goal record: the metric, its target, the done-standard and the budget (attempts, pieces and model calls) that Delegation and Model Plumbing enforce.
approach: Turn a request into a metric with a target value or improvement and a budget on the goal record, and roll the target of a sub-goal up to its parent objective, adjustable while the work runs.
out_of_scope: Creating the specs (ESOI Application does that), keeping the objectives (Objectives does that) and checking the result (Goal Completion does that).
milestones: 1. A request is turned into a metric with a target value or improvement that a reviewer accepts (authoritative metric metric-metric-translation).
measures_of_success: A request is turned into a metric with a target value or improvement that a reviewer accepts.
inputs: A request, and the parent target when there is one.
outputs: A metric with a target value or improvement for a request or a sub-goal.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("metric-translation", {"request": ...})` returns the target, its done-standard and its budget.

name: Response Quality
description: Judges a response against a quality profile: a named set of criteria with weights and target values. The profile is resolved for each request from the Representative, Guidance and Prioritization, and falls back to a default profile. The one arm today holds an answer to the evidence behind it, which covers faithfulness to evidence and nothing else.
purpose: Judge a response against the quality profile that applies to this request.
approach: Resolve the profile, judge each criterion, and report one balanced score per profile.
out_of_scope: A person's own profile (Representatives own that), context-specific criteria (Guidance owns those), translating implied priorities into weights (Prioritization owns that), updating a profile from feedback (Feedback Learning owns that) and whether the goal was met (Goal Completion).
milestones: 1. One balanced score for each quality profile, with the weights and targets of the profile fixed before any method is scored (authoritative metric metric-response-quality).
measures_of_success: One balanced score for each quality profile, with the weights and targets of the profile fixed before any method is scored.
inputs: A response, the evidence behind it and the resolved quality profile (the default profile when none is given).
outputs: The findings against each criterion of the profile; an empty list means the response held.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: One arm judges one criterion, faithfulness to the evidence; the other criteria of the default profile have no arm yet.

name: Context Intake
description: The one intake of the Mind. It takes what the Subconscious prepared from the system's internal context, what the World brought in and the instructions that apply to the request, and gives the Planner one view. Instructions are the third source: chosen for the request within a token budget so a task does not pay for rules it does not need, and counted in what the request costs.
purpose: Give the Planner one view of what is known for a request, whatever its source.
approach: Merge what was prepared, what the world brought and the instructions chosen for the request within a token budget into one labelled view, each line naming where it came from; picking information stays with the Subconscious.
out_of_scope: Finding or preparing the information, which is the Subconscious and the World.
milestones: 1. The Planner receives one view whatever the source of the information (authoritative metric metric-context-intake).
measures_of_success: The Planner receives one view whatever the source of the information.
inputs: A request, what the Subconscious prepared and what the World brought.
outputs: One view of the information for a request, its sources, and which instructions went in and how many tokens they cost.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("context-intake", {"request": ...})` returns the view; pass `instructions` (rules, a situation and a token budget) to add the third source.

name: Delegation
description: Hands each piece of work to the right worker, only when that is necessary. Every handoff carries the Representative's authority and a sub-goal with its own done-standard.
purpose: Hand work on without losing the authority it was given or the standard that says it is done, enforce the authority, the goal record's budget and cancellation (down to a running agent session), and refuse a piece it may not run with the reason.
approach: Hand each piece to the worker its category names only when a worker is needed, carrying the Representative's authority and the sub-goal's done-standard, enforce authority, budget and cancellation, and answer a piece that needs no worker from the view.
out_of_scope: Deciding the pieces (the Planner does that), checking the done-standard (Goal Completion does that), and carrying out the work (the tools do that).
milestones: 1. Each handoff names the authority it carries and a done-standard, and work is handed on only when necessary (authoritative metric metric-work-delegation).
measures_of_success: Each handoff names the authority it carries and a done-standard, and work is handed on only when necessary.
inputs: A piece, the Representative's authority and the sub-goal done-standard.
outputs: The result of a piece, from the worker that did it.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("delegation", {"pieces": [], "authority": {}})` returns one result per piece.

name: Planner
description: Breaks a request into pieces, each with the sub-goal it must meet and the worker category that fits it; on a replan it plans again only what failed. The arms are a rule router that reads the words of the request, a single-piece baseline and a model planner.
purpose: Turn a request into pieces that can be done and checked, each with the worker category that fits it, and replan from what failed.
approach: Break the request into pieces, each with the sub-goal it must meet and one worker category, and plan again only the pieces that failed when the goal was unmet; the arms differ in how they read the request (by its words, or by a model), not in what they return.
out_of_scope: Doing a piece (Delegation hands it on), and setting the target of the request (Metric Translation).
milestones: 1. Each piece of a request has a sub-goal that can be done and checked (authoritative metric metric-request-planner).
measures_of_success: Each piece of a request has a sub-goal that can be done and checked.
inputs: A request, its context, its target and the guidance, when there is some.
outputs: The pieces of a request, each with the sub-goal it must meet.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("planner", {"request": ...})` returns the pieces.
verdict_detail: cue_router is better than one_piece (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=3.38e-08, 63 of 105 cases disagree)

name: Response Writer
description: Outputs the plan, the request or the communication the Mind produced, in the form its reader needs and to the quality profile that applies.
purpose: Write what the Mind outputs for its reader.
approach: Write the reply from the results of the delegated pieces to the profile's criteria, saying plainly what a step could not do, and nothing a result did not hold.
out_of_scope: Judging the response against the quality profile (Response Quality does that) and deciding what to say (the Planner and workers do that).
milestones: 1. The written plan, request or communication meets the quality profile that applies (authoritative metric metric-response-writer).
measures_of_success: The written plan, request or communication meets the quality profile that applies.
inputs: The results of the pieces, the reader and the quality profile.
outputs: The written plan, request or communication.
effects: Reads and writes nothing itself: it calls the entry points of the parts it uses.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("response-writer", {"results": [], "profile": None})` returns the written text.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Cards From Files
description: Proposes a proportionate, current set of cards for material a consumer already keeps in files, without writing them.
purpose: Propose the cards a folder of files needs, in the card store record shape, for the Subconscious to keep and recall.
approach: Group the files that belong together, describe each group, and report which cards an edit has made stale.
out_of_scope: Keeping the cards (Card Store does that) and reading or writing files in general (Read Files and File Editing do that).
milestones: 1. The selected builder's balanced score on the mixed pinned cases is at least that of every free topic builder, with a store far below one card per file (metric-cards-from-files).
knowledge: Code graphs and repository maps group code by its call and import structure without a model; topic cards a model writes add the names a person would search for. A card groups information on one topic from many files and sources; a card per file is an index of files, so per_file_symbols and the degenerate groupings are baselines for file finding and never builders to ship. The earlier selection of per_file_symbols came from the file-finding metric, whose cases have one needed file each and so favour a card per file by construction; that metric alone was ill-posed for this solution. Its cases are now one kind of a mixed set with topic cases and a store-size term, and the selection is back on llm_topic_cards until that one number decides.
measures_of_success: The files a piece of work needed are inside the first cards the fixed selector picks, with little noise and with files of more than one folder bundled when the task spans them, from a store of at most 0.25 cards per file, at a price per build a team would pay.
parameters: The model provider, for a builder that calls one.
inputs: A folder root, the list of files to read, and the cards already kept for it.
outputs: Cards in the card-store record shape (grouping, summary, keywords, files with their hashes), and the ids of kept cards whose files changed.
effects: Reads files; writes nothing (the caller writes through card-store).
usage_notes: Run it for a first index and after edits, passing the cards already kept so a builder skips covered files. The per-file builder is the free floor; a builder that calls a model has to buy its price in accuracy on the balanced score. The per-file builder is a baseline for finding one file, not a card builder. The free topic builders (cochange_topic_cards, import_graph_topic_cards, the replay of the saved paid build) are scored for free; docs/how-to/iterate-on-card-builders-without-repeating-model-calls.md says how to iterate before any paid run.
verdict_detail: import_graph_topic_cards leads cochange_topic_cards (cochange_topic_cards 0.582 against import_graph_topic_cards 0.609; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.492, 90 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards leads file_plus_topic_cards (file_plus_topic_cards 0.299 against import_graph_topic_cards 0.609; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.362, 201 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than llm_topic_cards (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=3.68e-05, 247 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than one_card (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=9.59e-70, 241 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than one_card_per_folder (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=1.63e-36, 166 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards leads per_file_symbols (per_file_symbols 0.299 against import_graph_topic_cards 0.609; best guess, not yet significant, two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.492, 209 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than topic_cards_replay (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=0.00328, 225 of 252 cases disagree); import_graph_topic_cards is better than two_cards (two-sided exact sign test on per-case balanced scores, Holm-adjusted p=2.76e-70, 243 of 252 cases disagree)

name: Context Retriever
description: Cuts a corpus (files, the text of cards, or the turns of a conversation) into units at natural boundaries and returns, for a request, the units that answer it best first within a token budget, or nothing when the request needs no context. One retrieval for cards, file chunks and memory, measured on one balanced number.
purpose: Pick, from a corpus of files, cards or memory, the pieces of text a task needs within a token budget.
approach: Cut the corpus Internal Context returns into units, rank the units for the request and return the best within a token budget, or nothing when the request needs no context; every arm answers the same call and is scored on one balanced number.
out_of_scope: Formatting the picked text (the renderer where the picks are used does that) and offering what is not asked for (Intuition does that).
milestones: Lexical, latent, dense, fused, reranked, learned and abstaining arms recorded on one number over file, topic, orientation and no-context requests; a model reranker prepared for a recorded cassette.
knowledge: Retrieval papers favour hybrid first stages and rerankers; code retrieval gains from structure (names, imports, co-change); a consumer's own labelled history is the best training data and stays with the consumer.
measures_of_success: The balanced score of metric-context-retriever, which counts the recall of needed files within the budget, graded nDCG, the noise tokens shown, the size of the index, cost and time.
parameters: The budget in tokens, the corpus (a mapping of path to text) and an optional history of past changes; each arm's own settings are constructor arguments.
inputs: A request in words, and the files to retrieve from the first time.
outputs: Hits: unit id, file, first line, score, tokens and text, best first; an empty list means no context is needed.
effects: Reads the corpus it is given and keeps an index and a vector cache in the folder it is given; no network, and no model unless the arm is a model reranker.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("context-retriever", {"query": "where is the retry delay computed?", "files": {"net.py": "def retry_delay(attempt): ..."}})` returns the hits.

name: Research Freshness Reader
description: Reads the date each area of the registry was last researched and reports its age against a 90 day bar, naming the stale areas.
purpose: Read the registry's recorded dates and report how old each area's research is.
approach: Read the recorded research dates and report the days since each.
out_of_scope: Deciding which areas to research again (Learning does that) and doing the research.
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-research-freshness-reader has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: Every area's research age is read correctly.
parameters: clock: optional, so a test can fix the date.
inputs: An ISO date, or the registry facts together with a consumer's connections.

name: Model Tier Chooser
description: Picks, for each model tier, the provider and model that passes the most work per dollar on the same cases, counting prepaid credits as cost.
purpose: Pick, for each model tier, the model that does the most passing work per cost.
approach: Rank each provider and model by passing work per cost on shared cases and the prices on file.
out_of_scope: Calling the model (the Vendor Model Caller does that) and the wording of the question (each part does that).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-model-tier-chooser has a counting result for the arm.
measures_of_success: The chosen model per tier passes the most work per dollar on shared cases.
parameters: bars: optional keyword arguments that set the quality bars.
inputs: tiers (tier name to candidate arms with cases run, cases passed and tokens), prices (rows from the price file), optional credits and defaults.
outputs: A mapping from each tier to the chosen provider and model.
effects: None.
usage_notes: The default arm needs nothing from the consumer.
verdict_detail: no rival implementation was measured on the same cases

name: Vendor Model Caller
description: Plans, answers and lists models for one vendor, or for several through a router that steps to the next model when a provider fails.
purpose: Reach one vendor's model, and step to the next provider when one fails.
approach: Wrap each vendor behind one interface and route each call to the provider that serves its model, with a fallback when it fails.
out_of_scope: Choosing the tier (the Model Tier Chooser does that) and the wording of the question (each part does that).
milestones: Arms for the main vendors and the Claude Code program, a router that fails over, and recorded failover and answer checks.
knowledge: Each vendor's SDK and the claude program have their own limits, listed beside the arm in the requirements table.
measures_of_success: A call is answered when the primary provider fails, and a failure that is not the provider's is raised. Vendor answer quality is measured on model-tier-chooser (metric-vendor-answers).
parameters: Per vendor: key, base url, options and fallback models, all constructor arguments; nothing is read from the environment.
inputs: A model id and a prompt, or a planning request.
outputs: Text, a plan or a list of models.
effects: Network calls to the vendor; token totals are kept per calling thread.
usage_notes: The router (multi_provider) is the arm the failover metric selects and the one a consumer wires; the vendor adapters and the keyless claude_cli program are the providers it routes to, recorded as complementary arms of the call_a_model component and never ranked against it. What a subscription call costs counts inside the balanced number of the tier choice, not as a default typed into the selection.
verdict_detail: multi_provider is better than single_provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=7.63e-06, 18 of 30 cases disagree)

name: Connected System Operations
description: Calls an operation of a connected system, such as a write through an MCP server. A consumer that declares its own system's operations (for example a product's operations tool) supplies that as another alternative of the same job.
purpose: Carry out an operation of a connected system on the AI's behalf.
approach: Call one write operation of a connected system through its protocol, with the operation named by the goal, and report the result; nothing else is changed.
out_of_scope: Deciding to call it (the Planner and Delegation do that), the system's enduring integrations (Hands does that) and editing files (File Editing does that).
milestones: 1. A called operation does what was asked and nothing else (authoritative metric metric-connected-system-operations).
measures_of_success: A called operation does what was asked and nothing else.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: An operation and its arguments.
outputs: The result of the operation, or the reason it was declined.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run('connected-system-operations', {'goal': ..., 'brief': ...}); the model or writer the arm needs is a constructor argument the consumer provides.

name: Delegated Agent Sessions
description: Hands open-ended work to an agent that runs in its own session and reports back. The three arms today are Claude Code agents, which are coding-oriented agents used as general ones. A general agent that is not tied to coding, and a non-coding agent for tasks such as research or writing, are researched candidates with no arm yet.
purpose: Get open-ended work done by an agent in its own session.
approach: Hand the goal to an agent that runs in its own session under a written done-standard and a turn limit, and return what it reported and whether it met the goal.
out_of_scope: Editing a single file (File Editing does that), calling one operation (Connected System Operations does that) and deciding the pieces (the Planner does that).
milestones: 1. A coding goal counts as done only when its own written tests pass after the arm has run, with the tests restored by the harness (authoritative metric metric-delegated-agent-sessions).
measures_of_success: A general task that is not coding counts as done only when the agent's final report holds every expected fact, the run says it met the goal and the files are unchanged.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: A goal, a brief and its done-standard.
outputs: A result that says whether the goal was met, with the reason.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run('delegated-agent-sessions', {'goal': ..., 'brief': ...}); the model or writer the arm needs is a constructor argument the consumer provides.
verdict_detail: the selected implementation has no recorded row; best guess on the point estimate (none 0.3); no test was possible

name: File Editing
description: Changes a file by instruction and reports what changed. The alternatives do the same job at the same level: a one-call model edit and, as researched candidates with no arm yet, exact string replacement and patch formats.
purpose: Make the file change that was asked for, and no other.
approach: Land one bounded change to a file named by the goal in one model call, with the file read first and the change checked against it; nothing else is changed.
out_of_scope: Deciding what to change (the Planner does that), checking the goal (Goal Completion does that) and running open-ended agent work (Delegated Agent Sessions does that).
milestones: 1. A coding goal counts as done only when its own written tests pass after the arm has run, with the tests restored by the harness (authoritative metric metric-file-editing).
measures_of_success: A coding goal counts as done only when its own written tests pass after the arm has run, with the tests restored by the harness.
parameters: model, max_turns, run_id and context_preamble, all optional; the writer the arm may use is a constructor argument.
inputs: A file instruction and a folder it may write in.
outputs: A report of the file change, or the reason it was declined; nothing changes when it declines.
effects: Changes files or calls a write operation inside the writer the consumer grants; nothing changes when the arm declines.
usage_notes: Call hubofhubs.run('file-editing', {'goal': ..., 'brief': ...}); the model or writer the arm needs is a constructor argument the consumer provides. No consumer in this ecosystem wires a file writer today; retiring this solution is proposed.
verdict_detail: best guess, not yet significant: none 0.298 against fast_edit 0.972 on the point estimate; no case counts or per-case rows allow a test

name: File Reading
description: Lists and reads the text files of a folder, never outside it: the world-facing half of working with files that Cards From Files builds on.
purpose: Read the files a task or a card builder needs, without leaving the folder it was given.
approach: List the text files of one folder and read the ones asked for, never outside the folder and never more than a size cap, so one read cannot flood a context.
out_of_scope: Writing files (File Editing does that) and deciding which files matter (Cards From Files and the Context Retriever do that).
milestones: 1. Read the files a task or a card builder needs, without leaving the folder it was given. (authoritative metric metric-read-files).
measures_of_success: Read the files a task or a card builder needs, without leaving the folder it was given.
inputs: A folder, optionally paths and suffixes.
outputs: The file paths of a folder, and the text of the files asked for.
effects: Reads the folder; writes nothing.
usage_notes: `hubofhubs.run("read-files", {"root": ".", "paths": []})` reads the text files of a folder.

name: Web Search
description: One narrow call: a query in, a response of hits out. The hub ships thin adapters over open-source and hosted search services, and a consumer may provide its own.
purpose: Run one web search and return its hits with their sources.
approach: Send the query to the chosen service and return hits with a title, a link and a snippet.
out_of_scope: Public research papers (Science does that) and reading a person's own data (Internal Context declares where it is and File Reading reads it).
milestones: 1. The offline stage of metric-web-search has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 2. The live stage of metric-web-search has a counting result for at least two arms on the same cases. 3. The selected arm is the one the cascade of metric-web-search chooses (rule S33).
measures_of_success: Result rows with a title, a link and a snippet for a query.
parameters: The service address or API key of the chosen arm, a timeout and an optional daily limit.
inputs: A query, a result limit and an optional instruction for a model-backed arm.
outputs: A response of hits (title, link, snippet, date, passages and their kind), an optional direct answer and the queries issued; raises SearchBackendError on failure.
effects: One network request per search to the chosen service, counted against the daily limit when one is set.
usage_notes: The hub ships arms (searxng, serper, brave, tavily, gemini, provider) and a selector over them (hubofhubs.the_world.tools.web_search.backends.select_search_backend). None is selected by default: no metric run exists yet, so a consumer names an arm in its selections or provides its own object.
verdict_detail: gemini is better than provider (two-sided exact McNemar test, Holm-adjusted p=1.1e-05, 22 of 40 cases disagree)
